# Plugin API reference

<!-- Generated by docs/src/plugin-api.test.ts. Don't edit this file. Regenerate: bun --bun vitest run docs/src/plugin-api.test.ts -u -->

This page lists what a plugin can import from `@aphelion/plugin-sdk`, for plugin API version 0.2.2. A plugin's manifest names the plugin API versions it works with ([the API range](plugin-manifest.md#the-api-range)). A test generates this page from the types and doc comments in [`packages/plugin-sdk/src`](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/tree/main/packages/plugin-sdk/src) and fails when this page is out of date.

A `z.ZodType<T>` on this page is a [Zod](https://zod.dev/) schema. Its `parse` method checks a value and returns it as a `T`, or throws when the value doesn't match.

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk`

### `Cleanup`

A function that `start` can return. The SDK calls it once when the plugin shuts down, and logs an error if it throws.
It runs after the event handlers that were still running have finished, or after 3 seconds if one of them is still running.

```ts
type Cleanup = () => MaybePromise<void>;
```

### `ContributionKind`

The names of the lists in a manifest's `contributes`.

```ts
type ContributionKind = "secretSchemes" | "screens";
```

### `HostError`

The error that a call to the host rejects with when the host refuses it, such as `Not granted`.

```ts
class HostError extends Error {
  readonly code: number;
  constructor({ code, message }: RpcError);
}
```

- `code`: The JSON-RPC error code, such as `-32001`. `rpcErrors` lists every code the host sends.
- `constructor`: Makes the error from the error object in the host's reply.

### `ManifestIssue`

One problem that `parsePluginManifest` found.

```ts
type ManifestIssue = {
  field?: string;
  message: string;
};
```

- `field`: The field with the problem, such as `permissions.network[0]`. It is missing when the problem is with the whole manifest.
- `message`: What is wrong with the field, such as `is required`.

### `ManifestResult`

The result of `parsePluginManifest`. It holds the manifest when `ok` is `true`, and the problems when `ok` is `false`.

```ts
type ManifestResult =
  | {
      ok: true;
      manifest: PluginManifest;
    }
  | {
      ok: false;
      issues: ManifestIssue[];
    };
```

### `MaybePromise`

A value, or a promise of one.

```ts
type MaybePromise<T> = T | Promise<T>;
```

### `NetworkReply`

The host's reply to `network.get`.

```ts
interface NetworkReply {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly body: string;
}
```

- `status`: The HTTP status code.
- `body`: The response body as text. The host fails a response whose body is larger than 64 KiB.

### `PermissionKind`

The names of the lists in a manifest's `permissions`.

```ts
type PermissionKind = "events" | "secrets" | "network" | "uiSlots";
```

### `PluginContext`

The plugin's connection to the host, which `start` receives.

```ts
interface PluginContext {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly api: string;
  readonly events: {
    subscribe(
      name: string,
      handle: (data: unknown) => MaybePromise<void>,
    ): Promise<void>;
  };
  readonly network: {
    get(url: string): Promise<NetworkReply>;
  };
  readonly secrets: {
    use(operation: string, reference: SecretReference): Promise<void>;
  };
  log(message: string): void;
}
```

- `id`: The plugin's `id`, as the host sent it when it started the plugin.
- `api`: The plugin API version that the host runs, such as `0.2.2`.
- `events`: `subscribe(name, handle)` asks the host for an event, and the SDK then calls `handle` with each event's data.
  Once shutdown starts, the SDK calls no handler for a new event, and every call to the host fails with `the plugin is shutting down`.
  It rejects with a `HostError` when the manifest's `permissions.events` doesn't list the event or the owner hasn't granted it.
- `network`: `get(url)` asks the host to fetch an HTTPS URL that `requestUrl` accepts, from a host in `permissions.network` that the owner granted.
  The SDK sends one network or secret call at a time, so a second call waits until the first one has its reply.
- `secrets`: `use(operation, reference)` asks the host to run a named operation with a secret, such as a signed HTTP call.
  The plugin never receives the secret's value or the operation's result, and the call waits its turn like `network.get`.
  The deployed server runs no secret operations yet, so there a granted call fails with error `-32002`. `createTestHost` can run an operation that a test registers.
- `log`: Writes a message to the plugin's log, which goes to the server's log.

### `PluginIO`

The lines that `runPlugin` reads and writes. `main` builds one from standard input and output.

```ts
interface PluginIO {
  readonly input: AsyncIterable<string>;
  write(line: string): Promise<void>;
  log(message: string): void;
}
```

- `input`: The host's messages, one JSON line for each item.
- `write`: Sends one JSON line to the host, without its line break. The promise settles when the line is written.
- `log`: Writes a message to the log.

### `PluginManifest`

A manifest that `parsePluginManifest` accepted, read-only and with every list filled in.
A list that needs a part the plugin doesn't have is typed as empty, such as `uiSlots` for a plugin with only a server part.

```ts
type PluginManifest =
  | Readonly<
      Omit<
        {
          id: string;
          version: string;
          api: string;
          permissions: {
            events: string[];
            secrets: string[];
            network: string[];
            uiSlots: string[];
          };
          contributes: {
            secretSchemes: string[];
            screens: {
              id: string;
              title: string;
              icon?: string | undefined;
              menuOrder?: number | undefined;
            }[];
          };
          $schema?: string | undefined;
          repository?: string | undefined;
          server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
          client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
        },
        "permissions" | "contributes" | ("server" | "client")
      > & { server: { readonly entry: string } } & { client?: never } & {
        permissions: {
          readonly events: readonly string[];
          readonly secrets: readonly string[];
          readonly network: readonly string[];
          readonly uiSlots: readonly never[];
        };
        contributes: {
          readonly secretSchemes: readonly string[];
          readonly screens: readonly never[];
        };
      }
    >
  | Readonly<
      Omit<
        {
          id: string;
          version: string;
          api: string;
          permissions: {
            events: string[];
            secrets: string[];
            network: string[];
            uiSlots: string[];
          };
          contributes: {
            secretSchemes: string[];
            screens: {
              id: string;
              title: string;
              icon?: string | undefined;
              menuOrder?: number | undefined;
            }[];
          };
          $schema?: string | undefined;
          repository?: string | undefined;
          server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
          client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
        },
        "permissions" | "contributes" | ("server" | "client")
      > & { client: { readonly entry: string } } & { server?: never } & {
        permissions: {
          readonly events: readonly string[];
          readonly secrets: readonly never[];
          readonly network: readonly never[];
          readonly uiSlots: readonly string[];
        };
        contributes: {
          readonly secretSchemes: readonly never[];
          readonly screens: readonly Readonly<{
            id: string;
            title: string;
            icon?: string | undefined;
            menuOrder?: number | undefined;
          }>[];
        };
      }
    >
  | Readonly<
      Omit<
        {
          id: string;
          version: string;
          api: string;
          permissions: {
            events: string[];
            secrets: string[];
            network: string[];
            uiSlots: string[];
          };
          contributes: {
            secretSchemes: string[];
            screens: {
              id: string;
              title: string;
              icon?: string | undefined;
              menuOrder?: number | undefined;
            }[];
          };
          $schema?: string | undefined;
          repository?: string | undefined;
          server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
          client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
        },
        "permissions" | "contributes" | ("server" | "client")
      > & {
        server: { readonly entry: string };
        client: { readonly entry: string };
      } & {} & {
        permissions: {
          readonly events: readonly string[];
          readonly secrets: readonly string[];
          readonly network: readonly string[];
          readonly uiSlots: readonly string[];
        };
        contributes: {
          readonly secretSchemes: readonly string[];
          readonly screens: readonly Readonly<{
            id: string;
            title: string;
            icon?: string | undefined;
            menuOrder?: number | undefined;
          }>[];
        };
      }
    >;
```

### `PluginScreen`

A full page that a plugin's client part adds to the app's menu, from `contributes.screens`.

```ts
type PluginScreen = PluginManifest["contributes"]["screens"][number];
```

### `RpcError`

A JSON-RPC error object.

```ts
interface RpcError {
  readonly code: number;
  readonly message: string;
}
```

- `code`: The error code, such as `-32001`.
- `message`: A short text that says what went wrong, such as `Not granted`.

### `RpcId`

The id of a JSON-RPC request. A reply carries the id of its request.

```ts
type RpcId = string | number;
```

### `RpcMessage`

One JSON-RPC 2.0 message that `rpcMessageSchema` accepted.

```ts
type RpcMessage =
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; result: unknown }
  | {
      jsonrpc: "2.0";
      id: string | number | null;
      error: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown };
    };
```

### `SecretBackend`

What a secret backend plugin implements for the schemes it lists in `contributes.secretSchemes`. The deployed server doesn't call secret backends yet.

```ts
type SecretBackend = {
  resolve(reference: SecretReference): Promise<string>;
};
```

- `resolve`: Returns the secret's value for a reference, or throws if it can't. The value goes only to the secrets broker.

### `SecretReference`

A secret reference, such as `op://vault/item/field`. It is a scheme, then `://`, then the path.

```ts
type SecretReference = `${string}://${string}`;
```

### `ServerPlugin`

A plugin's server part. Pass it to `main` from `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/stdio`.

```ts
interface ServerPlugin {
  start(context: PluginContext): MaybePromise<void> | MaybePromise<Cleanup>;
}
```

- `start`: The SDK calls `start` once, after it has answered the host's `initialize` request.
  If `start` throws or rejects, the plugin stops with that error.
  At shutdown the SDK waits for `start` to finish before it runs the cleanup that `start` returned.

### `eventParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the host's `event` notification.

```ts
const eventParams: z.ZodType<{ name: string; data: unknown }>;
```

### `failure`

Builds a JSON-RPC error reply. The id is `null` when the request couldn't be read.

```ts
const failure: (
  id: RpcId | null,
  error: RpcError,
) => { jsonrpc: string; id: RpcId | null; error: RpcError };
```

### `initializeParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the host's `initialize` request.

```ts
const initializeParams: z.ZodType<{ api: string; plugin: string }>;
```

### `maxPluginLineBytes`

The most UTF-8 bytes one JSON line may hold, not counting the newline. The limit is 1 MiB.

```ts
const maxPluginLineBytes: number;
```

### `methods`

The JSON-RPC method names that the host and a plugin send.

```ts
const methods: {
  readonly initialize: "initialize";
  readonly event: "event";
  readonly shutdown: "shutdown";
  readonly subscribe: "events.subscribe";
  readonly networkGet: "network.get";
  readonly secretsUse: "secrets.use";
};
```

### `networkGetParams`

The Zod schema for the params of `network.get`. The URL is at most 4096 characters.

```ts
const networkGetParams: z.ZodType<{ url: string }>;
```

### `networkReply`

The Zod schema for the result of `network.get`.

```ts
const networkReply: z.ZodType<{ status: number; body: string }>;
```

### `notification`

Builds a JSON-RPC notification. It leaves out `params` when they are `undefined`.

```ts
const notification: (
  method: string,
  params?: unknown,
) =>
  | { jsonrpc: string; method: string; params?: never }
  | { jsonrpc: string; method: string; params: {} | null };
```

### `parsePluginManifest`

Checks the parsed JSON of `aphelion-plugin.json`, including its API range. It returns the problems instead of throwing.

```ts
function parsePluginManifest(data: unknown): ManifestResult;
```

### `pluginApiVersion`

The plugin API version that this SDK and the host run. A manifest's `api` range must include it.

```ts
const pluginApiVersion: "0.2.2";
```

### `pluginLineFits`

Whether `line`, without its newline, fits in `maxPluginLineBytes` as UTF-8.

```ts
function pluginLineFits(line: string): boolean;
```

### `pluginManifestFile`

The name of the manifest file in a plugin's folder.

```ts
const pluginManifestFile: "aphelion-plugin.json";
```

### `pluginManifestSchema`

The Zod schema for `aphelion-plugin.json`, whose fields [the plugin manifest reference](plugin-manifest.md) lists.
It fills in empty lists and checks that `api` is a valid version range, but not that the range includes `pluginApiVersion`. `parsePluginManifest` checks both.

```ts
const pluginManifestSchema: z.ZodType<{
  id: string;
  version: string;
  api: string;
  permissions: {
    events: string[];
    secrets: string[];
    network: string[];
    uiSlots: string[];
  };
  contributes: {
    secretSchemes: string[];
    screens: {
      id: string;
      title: string;
      icon?: string | undefined;
      menuOrder?: number | undefined;
    }[];
  };
  $schema?: string | undefined;
  repository?: string | undefined;
  server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
  client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
}>;
```

### `releaseArchiveName`

The name of the release asset that holds the plugin's `dist/` folder, as a plain ustar archive.

```ts
const releaseArchiveName: "aphelion-plugin.tar";
```

### `releaseBundleName`

The name of the release asset that holds the GitHub artifact attestation for `releaseArchiveName`.

```ts
const releaseBundleName: "aphelion-plugin.tar.sigstore.json";
```

### `request`

Builds a JSON-RPC request.

```ts
const request: (
  id: RpcId,
  method: string,
  params: unknown,
) => { jsonrpc: string; id: RpcId; method: string; params: unknown };
```

### `requestUrl`

Checks a URL's form for `network.get`, and returns the URL, or `undefined` if the form is wrong.
The URL must use `https:`, a hostname with a dot and no dot at the end, and the default port, with no user name, password or text after a `#`, and not an IP address. `network.get` also refuses a URL longer than 4096 characters and a host that isn't granted.

```ts
function requestUrl(text: string): URL | undefined;
```

### `rpcErrors`

The errors that the host replies with, by name.
[The plugin reference](plugins.md#errors) says when the host sends each one.

```ts
const rpcErrors: {
  readonly parse: { readonly code: -32700; readonly message: "Parse error" };
  readonly invalidRequest: {
    readonly code: -32600;
    readonly message: "Invalid request";
  };
  readonly methodNotFound: {
    readonly code: -32601;
    readonly message: "Method not found";
  };
  readonly invalidParams: {
    readonly code: -32602;
    readonly message: "Invalid params";
  };
  readonly notGranted: {
    readonly code: -32001;
    readonly message: "Not granted";
  };
  readonly noSecretOperations: {
    readonly code: -32002;
    readonly message: "The host doesn't offer secret operations yet";
  };
  readonly operationFailed: {
    readonly code: -32003;
    readonly message: "Operation failed";
  };
  readonly busy: {
    readonly code: -32004;
    readonly message: "Operation in progress";
  };
};
```

### `rpcMessageSchema`

The Zod schema for one JSON-RPC 2.0 message: a request, a notification, a success reply or an error reply. It refuses a field that the message type doesn't have.

```ts
const rpcMessageSchema: z.ZodType<
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; result: unknown }
  | {
      jsonrpc: "2.0";
      id: string | number | null;
      error: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown };
    }
>;
```

### `secretsUseParams`

The Zod schema for the params of `secrets.use`. The operation name is at most 128 characters, and the reference at most 1024.

```ts
const secretsUseParams: z.ZodType<{ operation: string; reference: string }>;
```

### `subscribeParams`

The Zod schema for the params of `events.subscribe`. The event name is at most 128 characters.

```ts
const subscribeParams: z.ZodType<{ event: string }>;
```

### `success`

Builds a JSON-RPC success reply.

```ts
const success: (
  id: RpcId,
  result: unknown,
) => { jsonrpc: string; id: RpcId; result: unknown };
```

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/runtime`

### `runPlugin`

Runs a plugin on the given lines until the host sends `shutdown` or closes its input. It then reads no more events, waits up to 3 seconds for event handlers that are still running, and runs the plugin's cleanup.
It rejects when the plugin's `start` fails before shutdown begins, or when reading or writing a line fails while the plugin runs. A `start` that fails after shutdown has begun is only logged. Most plugins call `main` instead.

```ts
function runPlugin(plugin: ServerPlugin, io: PluginIO): Promise<void>;
```

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/stdio`

### `main`

Runs a plugin on standard input and output, and exits the process when the plugin stops, with code 0, or 1 after an error.
It drops a line from the host that is longer than 1 MiB, and logs that it did.

```ts
function main(plugin: ServerPlugin): void;
```

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/testing`

### `CallOutcome`

The test host's answer to a request, which is a result or an error.

```ts
type CallOutcome =
  | {
      readonly result: unknown;
    }
  | {
      readonly error: {
        readonly code: number;
        readonly message: string;
      };
    };
```

### `FakeSecretOperation`

A secret operation that the test host runs for `secrets.use`.

```ts
interface FakeSecretOperation {
  readonly reference: SecretReference;
  readonly host: string;
  run(pluginId: string): MaybePromise<unknown>;
}
```

- `reference`: The secret reference that the plugin must name, and that the plugin needs a grant for.
- `host`: The hostname that the operation sends to. The plugin needs a network grant for it.
- `run`: Runs the operation with the plugin's id. The plugin never sees what it returns or throws, and the call fails after 5 seconds.

### `Grant`

A permission that the owner granted, for `TestHost.setGrants`.

```ts
interface Grant {
  readonly kind: "events" | "network" | "secrets";
  readonly name: string;
}
```

- `kind`: The manifest list in `permissions` that the permission is in.
- `name`: The event name, hostname or secret reference.

### `HostCall`

One request that the plugin sent to the test host.

```ts
interface HostCall {
  readonly method: string;
  readonly params: unknown;
  readonly outcome: CallOutcome;
}
```

- `method`: The JSON-RPC method, such as `network.get`.
- `params`: The params that the plugin sent.
- `outcome`: The test host's answer.

### `TestHost`

A fake host for a plugin's tests. It checks grants, network calls and secret operations the way the real host does.
Unlike the real host, it can run secret operations that a test registers with `registerSecretOperation`.

```ts
interface TestHost {
  setGrants(grants: readonly Grant[]): void;
  respondToGet(url: string, respond: () => MaybePromise<NetworkReply>): void;
  registerSecretOperation(name: string, operation: FakeSecretOperation): void;
  start(plugin: ServerPlugin): Promise<void>;
  publish(name: string, data: unknown): Promise<void>;
  stop(): Promise<void>;
  readonly logs: readonly string[];
  readonly calls: readonly HostCall[];
}
```

- `setGrants`: Sets what the owner granted, replacing earlier grants. A grant counts only when the manifest also lists the permission.
- `respondToGet`: Sets the reply to `network.get` for one URL. A URL with no reply, a reply that takes more than 5 seconds, and a body larger than 64 KiB fail with `Operation failed`.
- `registerSecretOperation`: Adds a named operation for `secrets.use`. While none is registered, `secrets.use` with a granted reference fails with error `-32002`.
- `start`: Starts the plugin and resolves when its `start` has finished, or rejects when `start` fails. A test host starts one plugin only.
- `publish`: Sends an event to the plugin and resolves when its handler has finished.
  It rejects when the encoded event line is longer than 1 MiB, as the real host does, and sends nothing.
  It sends nothing and resolves at once when the plugin isn't running, hasn't subscribed, or isn't granted the event, and from the moment `stop` is called.
- `stop`: Sends `shutdown` and resolves when the plugin has stopped. The SDK first waits up to 3 seconds for handlers that are still running, then runs the plugin's cleanup.
  A second call resolves when the first one does.
- `logs`: The messages that the plugin and the SDK logged, in order.
- `calls`: The requests that the plugin sent, with the answers, in the order the test host answered them.

### `createTestHost`

Makes a test host for a plugin's manifest, with nothing granted. It throws when the manifest is invalid or has no server part.

```ts
function createTestHost(manifestData: unknown): TestHost;
```
